dedupe_keys.name: geospatial network inventory free gni free qgis based ftth network design

description: GNI FREE is a free edition of the Geospatial Network Inventory telecom inventory system, built for operators and firms that plan, design and build fibre-to-the-home (FTTH) networks. It is a customised QGIS distribution that adds predefined layers, forms and symbology for network features, a set of free QGIS plugins and the vendor's own plugins, and stores data in a local SpatiaLite database shipped with it, using GRASS functions, public data and OpenStreetMap background maps. Its FTTH and GPON planner is a set of algorithms that guide the user from locating demand points and placing the optical line terminal, through clustering address points, proposing splice closure locations and cable routes, to choosing cable profiles and producing a resource report. Coverage: any area with address and street data. Format and access: Windows or QGIS installer from the vendor's download page, free of charge, with a paid full version adding inventory and operations functions. Caveats: design concepts only, from simple geometric clustering; the free edition's licence terms and update schedule were not checked. Simulation uses: capacity planning and cost optimisation of fibre access networks, and mapping fibre assets for hazard exposure. Related records: the national broadband maps give demand and coverage, and GNPy covers the optical transmission layer.
